props.title: Petroline and the Red Sea bypass
props.caption: Saudi Arabia's east-west oil line remained shut, leaving Yanbu loadouts and Bab el-Mandeb traffic as the physical test.
The talks concern reported Hormuz safe-route discussions, not yet a settled corridor.
The supported Record names Iraq's Shalamcheh order and a broader flight-and-crossing response after the Saudi drone attack.

items.note: The forecast turns on whether the shut Petroline leaves Yanbu loadouts and Bab el-Mandeb traffic visibly constrained by the next check.
Reported Hormuz safe-route talks leave corridor authority, fees and Washington's role unsettled.
Iraq's supported record names Shalamcheh and a broader flight-and-crossing clamp, but not the whole launch chain.
South Korea tracked short-range launches from Wonsan, with the mix of Hwasong-11 and 600 mm systems mattering more than range.

lead.what: The forecast asks whether public loadout or traffic evidence still shows a squeeze by 2026-09-13 at 18:00 UTC after the Petroline shutdown.

rest.what: Cogsworth puts the persistence call at 46%, noting that the record lacks segment damage, linefill loss, repair timing and a measured loadout drop.

lead.what: The Salalah record supports Hormuz safe-route talks and Iraq on the list, but not the date, binding terms, fees or Washington's role.

rest.what: The Iraq piece supports a flight suspension, border closures and Shalamcheh by name, while leaving the public launch trail unproved.

lead.what: The salvo's useful hardware fact is the reported Hwasong-11 and 600 mm mix, not a new range claim.

rest.what: The oil file supports Friday's $104.61 Brent settlement and an IEA report page, but not detailed Saudi production arithmetic.
